preamble: Loss of the close front vowel [i] typically affects short unstressed vowels, either word-internally (syncope) or word-finally (apocope). Vulgar Latin syncopated post-tonic i (calidus > caldus), and Proto-Norse lost unstressed *i after it had triggered i-umlaut (*gastiʀ > Old Norse gestr).

examples.note: Syncope of the unstressed post-tonic i; the syncopated form underlies Italian caldo and Spanish caldo.
Unstressed *i was lost after causing i-umlaut of a > e; cf. Gothic gasts, Old English ġiest.

sources: Adams, J. N. (2013). Social Variation and the Latin Language. Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511843433
